01 · The headline

The scale of transformation

The Ministry of Steel's 2025–26 Annual Report states that India had about 1 million tonnes of steel capacity at Independence, entirely in the private sector. India is now the world's second-largest crude-steel producer and the world's largest producer of sponge iron.

02 · The transformation

Six structural chapters of India's steel story

The report itself frames the journey around state-led capacity creation, liberalisation and deregulation, private-sector expansion, global competitiveness and the move toward technology and sustainability.

1947

Start with a viable but small base

Three principal steel plants — Tata Iron & Steel Company, Indian Iron & Steel Company and Visvesvaraya Iron & Steel Ltd. — plus a few EAF plants. Capacity was about 1 MT and the industry was entirely private.

MID-1950s → EARLY 1970s

Build national industrial capacity

Large integrated public-sector plants were established at Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela and Bokaro. The report notes that crude-steel production grew to nearly 15 MT from the ~1 MT early-Independence base, making India the 10th-largest steel producer at that stage.

1991–92

Liberalise and open the sector

Large-scale capacity was removed from the public-sector reservation; licensing was withdrawn subject to locational restrictions; pricing and distribution controls ended; private-sector participation increased; foreign investment and global technology access expanded.

2005

Set a competitiveness blueprint

National Steel Policy 2005 was introduced as a blueprint for a self-reliant and globally competitive sector, with emphasis on world-standard efficiency, productivity and diversified steel demand.

2017

Move toward technology-led competitiveness

National Steel Policy 2017 set a roadmap toward a technologically advanced and globally competitive industry, with focus on raw-material security, R&D, import dependency, productivity, quality and investment.

2021 → 2026

Scale, specialise and modernise

PLI for Specialty Steel, digitisation of mines, PM GatiShakti, R&D, recycling, safety and technology initiatives are layered onto a rapidly expanding production and capacity base.

04 · The industry changed shape

From a public-sector core to a broad private-sector ecosystem

Crude steel production by sector · 2024–25
Private sector127.953 MT · 84%
Public sector24.227 MT · 16%

The report's table shows the private-sector share rising from 81% in 2021–22 to 84% in 2024–25, while the public-sector share moved from 19% to 16%.

What liberalisation unlocked
Private investment→State-of-the-art capacity→Global technology→Competition
Visuals are embedded vector illustrations created for this page; no external image or network access is required.

The Ministry's historical account notes that after 1991–92, Essar Steel, Ispat Industries and Jindal Group established large private-sector plants; Tata Steel also expanded. Around 9 MT of new private-sector capacity based on state-of-the-art technology emerged in the period described.

“Capital, technology, and competition” became new engines of steel-sector scale.
05 · From tonnes to capability

The ecosystem is more than steelmaking

The report's current picture spans raw materials, beneficiation, sponge iron, pig iron, steelmaking, rolling, specialty products, recycling, logistics, and downstream demand.

06 · Technology & product complexity

India is not only making more steel — it is targeting more specialised steel

PLI for Specialty Steel
₹43,874 Cr
Committed investment
Already invested>₹22,000 Cr
Jobs created>13,000
Projects44 + 42

The first two PLI rounds attracted 44 projects from 19 participating companies and 42 projects from 25 companies. Categories include coated/plated steel, high-strength/wear-resistant steel, specialty rails, alloy steel, wires and electrical steel.

Research becomes an industrial capability
R&D projects supported since scheme inception75
Completed35
Industry-adopted technologies6

The supported R&D portfolio covers low/lean-grade ore and coal beneficiation, alternative ironmaking, steel-plant waste/slag utilisation, energy/resource efficiency and low-carbon technologies.

Digitisation is also moving upstream

The Ministry describes digitisation as an important element for optimising mining. A roadmap has been put in place for iron-ore mining, with digitalisation being adopted across operations to improve productivity, safety, transparency and logistics performance.

Mine planning→Operations data→Productivity→Safety→Traceability
07A · Value-chain mix

How India actually makes its steel

The Ministry of Steel reports three principal crude-steel process routes. In FY2024–25, BOF remained the largest contributor, while the induction-furnace route had also become a major part of the production mix.

10 · The intellectual takeaway

What the numbers really say

Scale

India moved from about 1 MT of steel capacity at Independence to more than 160 MT of annual crude-steel production today.

Structure

The industry moved from an entirely private pre-Independence base, through public-sector-led nation building, to a predominantly private-sector production ecosystem.

Capability

The agenda has widened from tonnes and capacity to specialty steel, R&D, digital mines, resource efficiency, recycling, logistics and low-carbon technologies.

The 2047 lens

India has built a globally significant steel industry since Independence. The next question is: what kind of metals ecosystem will it build by 2047?
